### Enable Entire CLI with Auto-Commit Strategy

Source: https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/main/README.md

Enables the Entire CLI in a repository using the 'auto-commit' strategy. This command sets up the necessary hooks and configurations for automatic commit management.

```bash
entire enable --strategy auto-commit
```

--------------------------------

### Entire CLI Configuration Settings

Source: https://context7.com/entireio/cli/llms.txt

Configuration for Entire CLI is managed through JSON files. '.entire/settings.json' contains project-specific settings committed to git, while '.entire/settings.local.json' holds local overrides and is gitignored.

```json
// .entire/settings.json (project settings, committed to git)
{
  "strategy": "manual-commit",
  "agent": "claude-code",
  "enabled": true,
  "strategy_options": {
    "push_sessions": true,
    "summarize": {
      "enabled": false
    }
  },
  "telemetry": true
}

// .entire/settings.local.json (local overrides, gitignored)
{
  "enabled": false,
  "log_level": "debug"
}
```

Source: https://context7.com/entireio/cli/llms.txt

To enable Entire CLI with the `auto-commit` strategy, run `entire enable --strategy auto-commit` within your project directory. This configuration will automatically create checkpoints after each AI agent response, ensuring that your development history is captured continuously. The output will indicate that hooks are installed and the project is configured for this automatic checkpointing strategy.

--------------------------------

Source: https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/main/README.md

Entire uses two configuration files located in the `.entire/` directory: `settings.json` and `settings.local.json`. The `settings.json` file is shared across the team and is typically committed to git. It contains project-wide settings such as the `strategy`, `agent`, and whether Entire is `enabled`. The `settings.local.json` file is for personal overrides and is gitignored by default. It can be used to configure local settings like `enabled` status or `log_level`.

### Enable Entire CLI with Force Reinstall

Source: https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/main/README.md

Enables the Entire CLI and forces a reinstallation of hooks, removing any existing Entire hooks before setting up new ones. This is useful for troubleshooting or updating configurations.

```bash
entire enable --force
```

--------------------------------

### Diagnose and Fix Stuck Sessions with Entire Doctor

Source: https://context7.com/entireio/cli/llms.txt

The 'doctor' command diagnoses and fixes issues with stuck Entire sessions. It checks for orphaned session state files, shadow branches without corresponding sessions, and corrupted metadata.

```bash
# Diagnose and fix issues with stuck sessions
entire doctor

# Checks for:
# - Orphaned session state files
# - Shadow branches without corresponding sessions
# - Corrupted metadata
```

--------------------------------

### Rewind to Previous Checkpoint

Source: https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/main/README.md

Command to revert your project to a previous saved state (checkpoint) within the current AI agent session. It displays available checkpoints and allows selection for restoration.

```bash
entire rewind
```

### Troubleshooting > Common Issues

Source: https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/main/README.md

If you encounter the error "Not a git repository", navigate to a Git repository first. If Entire is disabled, run `entire enable`. When "No rewind points found" occurs, work with Claude Code and commit (manual-commit) or wait for agent response (auto-commit). For "shadow branch conflict", run `entire reset --force`.

--------------------------------

### entireio/cli > PostToolUse[TodoWrite]

Source: https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/main/docs/architecture/claude-hooks-integration.md

The `PostToolUse[TodoWrite]` hook is invoked whenever a subagent updates its todo list, facilitating fine-grained, incremental checkpointing during subagent execution. It first checks for an active pre-task file to ensure it's operating within a subagent task context; otherwise, it skips silently. The hook then detects file changes by comparing the current git worktree status against the last checkpoint. If no changes are detected, it returns without creating a checkpoint. It extracts the content of the last completed todo item from the `tool_input.todos` array to use as the checkpoint description. A sequence number is obtained for the checkpoint, and then a `TaskCheckpointContext` is built with `IsIncremental: true` and the todo content. This context is used to save an incremental checkpoint via `strategy.SaveTaskCheckpoint`, resulting in a small commit that captures the progress.
